articles.title: Negative pressure wound therapy for the prevention of surgical site complications in emergency laparotomies: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are common after emergency laparotomy and are associated with substantial morbidity, prolonged recovery, and increased health care costs. Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has been increasingly used prophylactically on closed incisions in high-risk surgical patients; however, evidence supporting its effectiveness after emergency laparotomy remains heterogeneous. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to reassess the effectiveness of NPWT compared with standard postoperative dressings for the prevention of SSI and other wound-related complications following emergency laparotomy.

**MATERIALS AND METHODS**: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published from April 2, 2022, to December 10, 2025, updating a prior review. Randomized clinical trials and comparative observational studies evaluating NPWT versus standard dressings in adult patients undergoing emergency laparotomy were included. The primary outcome was SSI. Secondary outcomes included superficial and deep SSI, wound dehiscence, seroma, hematoma, and length of hospital stay. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE.

**RESULTS**: Twenty-three studies involving 5371 patients were included, of whom 2528 received NPWT. NPWT was associated with a significantly lower risk of SSI compared with standard dressings (risk ratio, 0.53; 95% CI 0.41-0.68), with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I² = 68%). NPWT was also associated with reductions in superficial and deep SSI, seroma formation, and wound dehiscence, but not with organ/space SSI, hematoma, or length of hospital stay. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent direction of effect. Funnel plot asymmetry and a significant Egger test suggested small-study effects.

**CONCLUSION**: Among patients undergoing emergency laparotomy, prophylactic NPWT applied to closed incisions was associated with a lower risk of SSI and several wound-related complications compared with standard postoperative dressings. However, the certainty of evidence remains very low due to heterogeneity, risk of bias, and small-study effects, highlighting the need for large pragmatic multicenter randomized trials to better define the magnitude of benefit and optimal patient selection.

Fatigue, Anxiety and Depression 12 Months After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Population Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
**AIM**: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms.

**METHODS**: This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work.

**RESULTS**: Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p<0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78;p<0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02,0.21;p=0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18;p<0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Fatigue, anxiety, and depression were common at 12 months after OHCA and are associated with poorer recovery. Fatigue exceeded population norms and may be an under-recognised component of cardiac arrest survivorship.

articles.title: Regional implementation of a prehospital advanced life support program with video-assisted physician direction and outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: The smart advanced life support (SALS) program was introduced to provide prehospital advanced life support under real-time video-assisted physician direction for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This study evaluated the association between regional SALS implementation and OHCA outcomes.

**METHODS**: This retrospective cohort study used difference-in-differences and event-study analyses with data from the OHCA surveillance system in South Korea and included adult OHCA cases (aged ≥19 years) from 2 years before through 4 years after SALS implementation in August 2015. The exposure was region-level implementation of SALS. Outcomes were the prehospital time interval, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to discharge, and favorable neurological outcome. Pre- to post-implementation changes were compared between regions with and without SALS.

**RESULTS**: A total of 129,207 cases were included. SALS regions had greater increases in the prehospital time interval (4.12 minutes; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.91 to 5.33) and prehospital ROSC (1.35 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.56 to 2.15) than regions without SALS. No significant additional improvements were observed in survival to discharge (-0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.31 to 0.62) or favorable neurological outcome (-0.35 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.08 to 0.37). Event-study analyses suggested differential pre-intervention trends for prehospital time, but not for the other outcomes.

**CONCLUSION**: SALS regions showed greater increases in prehospital time and prehospital ROSC without significant improvements in survival to discharge or favorable neurological outcome, but the finding for prehospital time should be interpreted cautiously because differential pre-intervention trends were observed.

articles.title: Moderate and Severe Traumatic Brain Injury Outcomes-A 20 Year (2002-2021) Analysis.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: Although recognised as a leading cause of death and disability, it is unclear whether current treatment strategies have improved outcomes from blunt moderate to severe traumatic brain injuries (msTBI) due to a lack of available epidemiological data. This study sought to determine if in-hospital mortality and early functional outcomes of msTBI patients have changed over 20 years. Early functional outcomes were determined through the surrogate measure of the proportion of patients discharged directly to home.

**METHODS**: A longitudinal cohort study using The Alfred Health Trauma Registry data. Subjects were aged 16-70 years with blunt msTBI (Head Abbreviated Injury Scale 3-5) admitted to The Alfred Trauma Service between 1 January 2002 and 31 December 2021.

**RESULTS**: A total of 8222 patients presented with msTBI over the period, with 692 deaths (8.5%). Unadjusted in-hospital mortality decreased from 12.1% in 2002 to 4.0% in 2021 (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.95-0.97, p < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the odds of death even after adjusting for injury severity (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.99, p < 0.0001). The proportion of patients discharged to home increased from 30.6% to 60.8% over the period (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.04-1.06, p < 0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: There was a reduction in in-hospital mortality and an increase in the proportion discharged home for adults hospitalised with msTBI at The Alfred Hospital over the last two decades. These results foster optimism for the care of neurotrauma patients, but further research is required to identify the modifiable factors associated with these improved outcomes.

articles.title: Bezoar ileus in patients with previous abdominal surgery: an observational comparison of conservative and surgical management.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Evidence on the management of bezoar ileus in patients who have already undergone abdominal surgery is limited. We reviewed conservative and surgical pathways in clinically selected patients, with particular attention to patient selection criteria and how each pathway was defined.

**METHODS**: We reviewed 80 patients with CT-confirmed bezoar ileus and previous abdominal surgery who were treated between January 2010 and December 2021. Twenty-six completed conservative treatment, and 54 underwent surgery. In practice, conservative treatment was used for clinically stable patients without peritonitis or CT signs suggesting ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, provided that close clinical monitoring was possible. Conservative treatment included bowel rest, intravenous fluids, electrolyte correction, symptom-directed medication and nasogastric decompression when needed. Failure was defined by clinical deterioration, persistent or worsening obstruction, inability to tolerate oral intake, or new radiological concern. The primary outcome was clinical resolution during the index admission. Secondary outcomes were hospitalisation, in-hospital mortality, postoperative complications and readmission after discharge.

**RESULTS**: The treatment groups were not equivalent at baseline. Patients treated surgically more often had gastric bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 0/26, p = 0.002), multiple bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 1/26, 3.8%, p = 0.009) and greater small-bowel dilatation (median 4.0 cm vs. 3.4 cm, p = 0.014). All 26 patients in the conservative pathway completed the index admission without operation, although routine radiological confirmation of resolution was not performed. Median hospitalisation was 4 days (IQR 4-5) in the surgical group and 7 days (6-8) in the conservative group (p < 0.001); this difference should be interpreted in the context of clinical selection and local practice. Postoperative complications occurred in 11/54 surgical patients (20.4%), including two deaths from pulmonary embolism. Among discharged patients, readmission did not differ significantly between groups (13/52, 25.0% after surgery vs. 5/26, 19.2% after conservative treatment; p = 0.776). Exploratory regression findings were treated as hypothesis-generating only.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Conservative treatment may be feasible in selected stable patients with bezoar ileus after previous abdominal surgery. Surgery remains appropriate for patients with peritonitis, suspected ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, clinical deterioration, or failure of conservative management. Because treatment was not protocolised and the groups differed at baseline, the findings should be read as observational and hypothesis-generating, not as evidence that either strategy is superior.

articles.title: Low-Titer O + Whole Blood Implementation in the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City and Tulsa: Significance, Success, & Sharing Lessons Learned.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Over 300 emergency medical services (EMS) organizations across the United States have implemented transfusion programs for traumatic injuries using packed red blood cells, platelets, plasma, or whole blood before hospital arrival. Beginning in December of 2022, the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City (OKC) and Tulsa began carrying low-titer O-positive whole blood (LTOWB) for adult patients in traumatic hemorrhagic shock, specifically those exhibiting elevated shock indexes. We aim to describe establishing our prehospital LTOWB program and its first two years of operations across OKC and Tulsa.

**METHODS**: We used an observational study design and retrospective descriptive analysis of patients receiving LTOWB by paramedic transfusion from the Emergency Medical Services Authority Ambulance Service, Oklahoma City Fire Department, or Tulsa Fire Department between December 1, 2022, and February 1, 2025. Descriptive analysis and univariate logistic regression quantify the relationship of patient characteristics against survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge outcomes.

**RESULTS**: Penetrating trauma was the most common mechanism of injury recorded for patients receiving EMS LTOWB (71.6%). Following LTOWB transfusion, prehospital vital signs (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index) significantly improved (p < 0.05). Systolic blood pressure improvement conferred 9.7 times greater odds of survival to hospital arrival (95% CL 1.6-58.6). Occurrence of prehospital traumatic circulatory arrest was significantly related to lower odds of survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge (OR 1.01 and OR 1.04, respectively).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Transfusion of LTOWB in a large, urban EMS system in the Southwestern United States confers a positive benefit to patients with measurable improvement in median systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index. Continuous review of cases and misses empowered our system in dynamic protocol adjustments to best meet our population's needs. Patients often had secondary deterioration during transit, illustrating that blood transfusion "bought" temporary time during transport of critically injured patients to definitive care.

articles.title: Weathering the storm: Predictors and resource burden of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity after severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Reported incidence of paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) after severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) approaches one-third, largely from cohorts that excluded early deaths. Predictors and resource consequences remain unclear. We identified predictors of PSH development and associations between diagnosis, PSH Assessment Measure (PSH-AM) subscores [clinical features scale (CFS) and diagnosis likelihood tool (DLT)], and resource utilization.

**METHODS**: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with severe TBI admitted to a tertiary care center intensive care unit (ICU) (October 2020-September 2025), stratified by PSH diagnosis. Two reviewers assigned PSH-AM scores. PSH cannot be diagnosed until the syndrome declares itself over days, so exposure is conditioned on survival; mortality is reported descriptively. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of PSH diagnosis. Log-transformed linear regressions estimated associations of PSH diagnosis and subscores with hospital length of stay (LOS), ICU LOS, and ventilator days. Thirty-day composite outcomes, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and landmark analysis evaluated robustness.

**RESULTS**: Of 509 patients with severe TBI, 86 (17%) developed PSH. Younger age [odds ratio (OR): 0.97 (95% CI: 0.96-0.98); P<0.001) and higher ISS [1.05 (1.02-1.07); P<0.001] independently predicted PSH. PSH was associated with longer hospital LOS (372.9%), ICU LOS (278.3%), and more ventilator days (266.4%; all P<0.001). Mortality was 11.6% (PSH) versus 35.9% (non-PSH). IPTW demonstrated PSH had fewer days alive and out of hospital (-46.8%; P<0.001) and landmark analysis highlighted fewer ventilator-free days (-40.2%; P=0.0097) and ICU-free days (-46.9%; P<0.001). Higher DLT subscores were associated with longer hospital (36.3%; P=0.001) and ICU (23.3%; P=0.005) stays, whereas the CFS subscore showed no associations.

**CONCLUSIONS**: The PSH diagnosis is contingent on survival. Younger patients with severe TBI who survive their initial injuries are more likely to develop PSH and occupy hospital beds meaningfully longer. The diagnosis likelihood tool, not the clinical features scale, tracks with that burden.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Wrong hospital, wrong outcome: Impact of care fragmentation following trauma laparotomy.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Care fragmentation (CF), defined as readmission to a nonindex hospital, has been identified as a potential predictor of poor outcomes after traumatic injury. Trauma laparotomy (TL) is a common procedure with perioperative risk of complications and readmission. Incidence of CF following TL, its risk factors, and its effects on outcomes are unknown. We hypothesized that CF after TL is associated with increased mortality during hospital readmission compared with continuity of care (CC).

**METHODS**: The Nationwide Readmissions Database (2016-2022) was queried for hospitalized adult (≥18) patients with traumatic injury and open surgery of gastrointestinal or genitourinary systems during index admission, and unplanned readmission within 90 days. Demographics, comorbidities, injury severity, procedures, and disposition data were collected for patients with CF and compared with patients with CC. The primary outcome was in-hospital death during readmission. Univariate comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

**RESULTS**: A total of 14,773 TL patients were included in the analysis. From these, 2,059 (13.9%) were readmitted within 90 days. The average age of readmitted patients was 43 years, and the majority (68.6%) were male. Of the readmissions, 441 (21.4%) experienced CF. Discharge home from the index admission was associated with lower odds of CF (OR 0.52, 95% CI: 0.32-0.84, p=0.008). On multivariable regression analysis, CF was significantly associated with in-hospital death during readmission (OR 5.09, 95% CI: 1.22-21.16, p=0.03).

**CONCLUSIONS**: CF is common following TL and is associated with an increased risk of death on readmission, even after adjustment for baseline comorbidities and other hospital characteristics. Patients who are discharged home are less likely to experience CF. TL survivors may represent a patient population that would benefit from targeted efforts to reduce CF.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Therapeutic; Level III.

articles.title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain.

**MATERIALS & METHODS**: Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality.

**RESULTS**: The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality.

**CONCLUSION**: The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

articles.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma.

**METHODS**: A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge."

**RESULTS**: Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge.

**CONCLUSIONS**: The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

articles.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system.

**METHODS**: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models.

**RESULTS**: Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay.

**TRIAL REGISTRATION**: Not applicable.

Incidence of severe mountain bike-related injuries and mortality: A 15-year statewide analysis.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Mountain biking has grown in popularity and has seen widespread trail development but carries risk for severe trauma. No studies have analysed severe injuries in the context of contemporary mountain biking to understand trends and modifiable risk factors.

**AIM**: To describe the incidence and longitudinal characteristics of severe injuries related to mountain biking in Tasmania, Australia.

**METHODS**: Retrospective analysis of all patients admitted to Tasmanian public hospitals with severe mountain bike (MTB)-related injuries from 1st January 2010-31 st December 2024.

**MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES**: Incidence of severe MTB-related injuries (including mortality) as defined by hospital admission to an intensive care unit or neurosurgery high dependency unit; for emergency surgery (in <4 h); or transfer intra- or interstate for definitive treatment. Secondary outcomes were annual injury trends in mechanism of injury, body regions, injury profiles, and incident location.

**RESULTS**: For the total period there were 85 severe injuries (including 4 mortalities) from 6643 MTB-related emergency department (ED) presentations. Annual severe MTB-related cases increased over the 15 years from 0.8 cases/year before 2015, to 8.1 cases/year in later years. Severe injury cases accounted for only 1.3% of all MTB-related ED presentations. Most severely injured riders were male (97%); the mean age was 36 years (SD 16.9) for the total period, but this increased from 18.5 years (SD 5.8) pre-2015-36.9 years (SD 16.8) post-2015. Executing a jump was the dominant mechanism of injury (44%), followed by fall over handlebars (14%), obstacle collision (11%) and adverse trail conditions (9%). The most injured body regions were abdomen (31%), neck (23%) and thorax/chest (20%). The most common types of injuries were fracture/dislocation (44%), abdominal organ injury (24%) and thoracic organ injury (15%). Spinal cord injury occurred in 6% of cases and traumatic brain injury in 7%. Over 50% of severe injury incidents occurred on purpose-built MTB trails.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Severe MTB-related injuries increased proportionally to all MTB-related injuries suggesting the increase was largely driven by rider exposure. Targeted injury prevention strategies, safe trail design, and understanding risk factors are needed to ensure safe progression of this popular sport.

articles.title: Adjunct rim plating for selected pilon fracture patterns: Lessons from hyperextension tibial plateau fractures.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Pilon fractures frequently involve small anterior or anterolateral marginal fragments that are susceptible to shear displacement and may not be reliably controlled by conventional periarticular plates. Rim plating is a fragment-specific, low-profile juxta-articular buttress technique that has demonstrated favorable biomechanical and clinical results in selected tibial plateau fracture patterns. This review examines the rationale for extending this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns.

**METHODS**: We performed a narrative review of clinical, cadaveric, and biomechanical studies describing rim-based constructs in tibial plateau fractures, with emphasis on hyperextension and posterolateral patterns, as well as computed tomography (CT)-based studies of pilon fracture morphology and fragment capture by precontoured plates. Relevant studies were identified through PubMed and reference screening and synthesized qualitatively to inform a technical proposal for adjunct rim plating in selected pilon fractures.

**RESULTS**: The reviewed tibial plateau literature consistently identified peripheral regions that may remain unsupported by conventional periarticular plates, particularly in hyperextension and posterolateral fracture patterns, where adjunct rim plating has been associated with maintained reduction and favorable clinical outcomes. In the distal tibia, CT-based studies suggest that commonly used anatomically precontoured plates may not reliably capture the anterolateral (Tillaux-Chaput) fragment when fragment height is less than 15 mm. In this setting, an adjunct rim plate may serve as a peripheral buttress to improve support of the articular margin, distribute subchondral stress, and prevent displacement of the articular block.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Rim plating may be best conceptualized as a joint-line buttress strategy for improving peripheral containment of shear-dominant marginal fragments. Extrapolation of this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns is mechanically plausible and supported indirectly by CT-based fragment-capture data. This technique may be useful in carefully selected anterior or anterolateral distal tibial rim fractures that are not adequately controlled by standard periarticular plating.

articles.title: Penetrating renal trauma in a high-complexity Latin American centre: Management patterns and renal preservation, 2013-2025 - a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Contemporary renal-trauma practice rests on blunt-predominant cohorts from high-income trauma systems, and penetrating renal injury remains under-described. We characterised the management and outcomes of penetrating renal trauma at a high-complexity Latin American centre, with blunt injury as internal comparator, and examined how practice changed over 13 years.

**METHODS**: Retrospective cohort of 161 consecutive adults (≥18 years) treated between February 2013 and July 2025, classified by mechanism. Management, nephrectomy and in-hospital outcomes are reported descriptively as n (%) and median [IQR]. Testing was confined to three pre-specified questions: whether nephrectomy differed by mechanism; whether it differed by mechanism among patients taken to open surgery; and whether it changed over time. Two-sided exact p values were obtained by doubling the one-sided probability.

**RESULTS**: Thirty-four injuries (21%) were penetrating (27 gunshot, 6 stab, 1 unspecified) and 126 (78%) blunt. Among penetrating injuries, 13 (38%) were managed non-operatively, 3 (9%) with angioembolisation and 18 (53%) with open surgery. Non-operative management was used up to AAST grade IV and failed in none, with no reintervention, nephrectomy or renal complication; angioembolisation preserved every treated kidney. Twelve of the 34 penetrating injuries (35%) ended in nephrectomy versus 5 of 126 blunt (4%; p < 0.001), and every nephrectomy in the cohort followed open surgery. Among the patients taken to open surgery, however, nephrectomy was equally frequent in the two groups (12 of 18 vs 5 of 9; p = 0.88), so renal loss tracked the decision to operate rather than intraoperative salvageability. High-grade (AAST IV-V) injury was similarly frequent by mechanism (41% vs 29%). Within penetrating injuries, open surgery fell from 15 of 24 in 2013-2019-3 of 10 in 2020-2025, and nephrectomy from 11 of 24-1 of 10, with a stable mechanism mix.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Selective non-operative management and angioembolisation preserved every kidney in which they were used, including after penetrating injury, and renal loss followed the decision to operate rather than the mechanism itself. These data support extending physiology-guided, kidney-preserving management to penetrating renal injury.

articles.title: Surgeon preferences and educational gaps in the treatment of complex distal radius fractures in Latin America.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Distal radius fractures are among the most common skeletal injuries, yet their optimal treatment remains controversial. Variability in surgical decision-making has been observed among surgeons. This study aimed to identify treatment preferences among Latin American orthopaedic surgeons with different training backgrounds and levels of experience in the management of complex distal radius fractures.

**METHODS**: A two-part questionnaire was distributed to orthopaedic and hand surgeons across Latin America. The first section collected demographic data, and the second section presented 7 clinical scenarios involving complex distal radius fractures. Multivariate analysis using multinomial logistic regression was performed to assess the influence of age and fellowship training on treatment decision-making, with results expressed as odds ratios. P-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

**RESULTS**: A total of 617 completed questionnaires were analyzed. Most respondents were male orthopaedic surgeons with fellowship training in orthopaedic trauma or hand surgery. Most surgeons reported managing 10-25 distal radius fracture cases annually as the lead surgeon and had access to both anatomical angle-stable volar plates and fragment-specific implants. Older surgeons tended to favor more traditional techniques, whereas those with hand surgery fellowship training were more likely to adopt advanced fixation strategies and a broader range of surgical approaches.

**CONCLUSION**: Surgeon age and fellowship training in hand surgery were the most influential factors in treatment decision-making for complex distal radius fractures. These findings highlight an opportunity for AO Trauma Latin America to expand educational offerings focused on the treatment of complex distal radius fractures.

articles.title: Trends in mortality rates in hypotensive pediatric trauma patients undergoing emergent trauma laparotomy.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Massive hemorrhage remains the leading cause of preventable death after pediatric trauma. Emergent trauma laparotomy (ETL) is a common operation to obtain hemorrhage control. Mortality rates for adult patients in hemorrhagic shock requiring ETL remain high and unchanged. Information on mortality rates after ETL in pediatric patients is limited. We sought to evaluate trends in mortality rates for pediatric ETL patients.

**METHODS**: The National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB) was queried from 2007 to 2023. Patients aged 0 to 18 years old were included if they underwent ETL. ETL was defined as laparotomy within 1 hour of arrival. Hypotension was defined as a systolic blood pressure <90 mm Hg on arrival. The primary outcome was annual hospital mortality rates for hypotensive patients requiring ETL. Secondary outcomes included annual 24-hour mortality rates for both hypotensive and all patients requiring ETL. Mortality rates were compared in 5-year cohorts to reduce annual variability.

**RESULTS**: A total of 11,374 patients underwent ETL. The majority of patients were male (79%; n=78,963/11,374). Most patients were between the ages of 12 and 17 (84%; n=9,565/11,374), followed by ages 5 to 11 (11%; n=1,227/11,374), then ages 0 to 4 (5%; n=582/11,374). Penetrating injuries predominated (69%; n=7,866/11,374). The hospital mortality rate for all patients was 18.3% (n=2,079/11,374). Of patients who died, 74% were within 24 hours of arrival (n=1,533/2,079). Overall, 19% (n=2,125/11,374) were hypotensive on arrival. For hypotensive patients, the 24-hour and hospital mortality rates were 30% (n=641/2,125) and 45.9% (n=976/2,125). There was year-to-year variability in rates of hospital mortality of hypotensive patients through the study period (p<0.001). However, the average mortality rates from 2007 to 2011 (45%; n=293/645) and 2019 to 2023 (42%; n=266/638) were unchanged (p=0.95).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Pediatric trauma patients with exsanguinating hemorrhage requiring ETL continue to suffer high rates of mortality. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted research and performance improvement.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Prognostic and Epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: Opioid prescribing and hospital outcomes after trauma in patients with substance use disorder: An analysis of the michigan trauma quality improvement project.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Trauma patients frequently have comorbid substance use disorders (SUD), which may complicate pain management and increase the risk of opioid-related adverse outcomes after discharge. We hypothesized that trauma patients with SUD would be prescribed more opioids at discharge than those without SUD.

**METHODS**: We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of adult trauma patients across the state from 2022 to 2025 using a statewide collaborative database. Primary outcomes were opioid prescription at discharge (yes/no) and amount prescribed standardized to oxycodone 5 mg pills. A multivariable approach assessed risk-adjusted differences in outcomes among patients with SUD versus without SUD.

**RESULTS**: Among 29,805 total patients, 8,672 (29.1%) had a diagnosis of SUD. 71.2% of patients with SUD received a discharge opioid prescription, compared with 59.6% of patients without SUD (p<0.001). After adjustment, the predicted probability of receiving an opioid prescription at discharge was 64.2% (95% CI, 63.1%-65.2%) for patients with SUD and 62.5% (95% CI, 62.0%-63.1%) for those without. Among patients that received a prescription, those with SUD were prescribed 21.2 pills of 5 mg oxycodone, corresponding to an adjusted difference of 1.6 additional pills (95% CI, 0.89-2.31; p<0.001) compared with those without. Prescribing patterns also differed by race and ethnicity: Hispanic or Latino patients were 5.4-percentage points more likely to receive an opioid prescription than non-Hispanic or Latino patients, while, among prescription recipients, Black patients received 3.56 fewer pills than White patients.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Our findings demonstrate that patients with SUD received opioids more frequently and in greater amounts at discharge, yet absolute differences were small in magnitude and may not represent clinically meaningful differences. Differences in prescribing by race and ethnicity were larger in magnitude and warrant further investigation.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Prognostic and epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: In older adults, "mild" by GCS does not mean low risk: Multicenter study of 1,157 patients with mild TBI and acute subdural hematoma.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Acute traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) is the most common intracranial injury in mild TBI (mTBI), particularly in older adults. However, the relationship of patient and brain computed tomography (CT) characteristics with outcomes remains poorly described in a contemporary cohort. This study aims to characterize outcomes in younger and older adults with mTBI and isolated acute SDH.

**METHODS**: This was a 10-center, retrospective cohort study of adult traumas with emergency department Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 13 to 15 and acute traumatic SDH on initial brain CT ('22-'23). Trauma registry, EHR, and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) data were collected through automated and manual methods. The primary outcome was total mortality (TM=death+hospice discharge); the sample was stratified by 18 to 64 versus older than or equal to 65 years. Multivariable backward selection logistic regression examined 21 demographic, injury, and brain CT covariates.

**RESULTS**: In total, 1,157 patients were included (18-64 y: 28%; ≥65 y: 72%; 58% transferred in). Median [IQR] non-head ISS was 1 [1-5] in 18 to 64 years, and 1 [1-2] in older than or equal to 65 years. Ten percent had neurosurgical intervention (18-64 y: 8%; ≥65 y: 11%). TM was higher in older than or equal to 65 years than 18 to 64 years (10% vs. 3%). Compared with older than or equal to 65 years, 18 to 64 years were discharged home more frequently (78% vs. 51%) and to hospice less frequently (2% vs. 7%). In 18 to 64 years, factors associated with TM were race, advance directive, functional dependence, ISS, more midline shift, and thicker SDH (too few TMs for adjusted models). In older than or equal to 65 years, factors independently associated with TM were advance directive (aOR [95% CI]: 11.8 [2.9-49.0]), male sex (3.0 [1.3-7.0]), midline shift (1.8 [1.3-2.6]), shock index (1.5 [1.1-2.1]), and worsening SDH on follow-up CT (2.9 [1.3-6.6]).

**CONCLUSIONS**: Despite presenting as "mild", these data highlight that older adults with SDH have high TM and should continue to receive the highest-level care with timely goals-of-care discussions. The association between advance directives and TM should be interpreted within the context of baseline vulnerability and preinjury treatment preferences, not as a biological mortality predictor.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Prehospital Risk Stratification for Early Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVES**: Pediatric criteria remain limited for identifying injured children who may benefit from early blood transfusion for hemorrhagic shock. This study evaluated whether emergency medical services (EMS)-observable variables in a national trauma registry could identify children at risk for early hospital blood transfusion.

**METHODS**: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study using the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2020). Among 391,126 records for patients aged 1-15 years, we included children transported by EMS directly from the scene to a participating trauma center after excluding burn injuries, interfacility transfers, and missing pre-identified EMS variables (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, or Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]). The primary outcome was any blood product administered within 4 hours of emergency department arrival. Five prespecified EMS-observable predictors composed the model: age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest. We fit a multivariable logistic regression and a classification and regression tree (CART) using an 80/20 stratified train-validation split. Missing data sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and CART refitting in the broader eligible cohort.

**RESULTS**: Among 79,764 children, 2,634 (3.3%) received early transfusion in the hospital. All five predictors were independently associated with early transfusion, led by GCS ≤14 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.61-9.22), penetrating mechanism (aOR 5.87; 95% CI, 5.28-6.51), and age-adjusted hypotension (aOR 5.39; 95% CI, 4.74-6.13). In the validation cohort, CART analysis stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk tiers comprising 77.0%, 19.7%, and 3.3% of patients, respectively. Early-transfusion rates were 1.2%, 6.1%, and 36.7% across these tiers. The high-risk tier accounted for 36.8% of all early transfusion events. Using the high-risk tier as a decision threshold, sensitivity was 36.8%, specificity 97.8%, positive predictive value 36.7%, and negative predictive value 97.8%.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Five EMS-observable features, including age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest, identified a small subgroup of pediatric trauma patients with substantially elevated risk of early hospital transfusion. This parsimonious framework may inform prospective validation of prehospital transfusion criteria.

articles.title: A Mixed Methods Evaluation of a Model of Care for Domestic Violence Within the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
**OBJECTIVE**: To describe the scope and extent of the Domestic Violence (DV) Model of Care at Campbelltown Emergency Department (ED). We detail patient population characteristics, means of identifying victim-survivors, care provided, and factors associated with social work review.

**METHODS**: This mixed-methods evaluation utilised (1) retrospective audits of medical records of patients admitted to Campbelltown ED in 2024, who (a) responded affirmatively on the DV Routine Screening (DVRS) tool, and/or (b) were reviewed by social work relating to DV; and (2) semi-structured interviews with 19 clinicians and support workers about their understanding of and role within the model of care. Descriptive analyses quantified the scope and characteristics of the DV patient population and care provision; logistic regression identified factors associated with DVRS-identified patients seeing social work. Thematic analysis of interview data supplemented audit findings.

**RESULTS**: In 2024, 249 ED patients responded affirmatively to the DVRS tool (DV identified prior for 52.2%), and 231 patients were reviewed by social work relating to DV. Victim-survivors were identified through DVRS tool use, explicit disclosure, referral from community partners, and clinician judgement. Transfer to the ED short stay unit facilitated safety and trauma/violence-informed care, including social work consultation for 49.8% of identified victim-survivors. Explicit disclosure or help-seeking, presenting concerns, and child safety risks were associated with seeing social work; however, presentation day/time was not.

**CONCLUSIONS**: This evaluation demonstrates that a comprehensive ED model of care, employing multiple means of identifying victim-survivors, is able to facilitate trauma/violence-informed psychosocial care alongside medical management for patients experiencing DV.

articles.title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure.

**METHODS**: A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure.

**RESULTS**: A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity.

**CONCLUSION**: We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

articles.title: Emergency medicine pharmacotherapy literature of 2025.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize pharmacotherapy-related emergency medicine (EM) literature indexed in 2025. Articles were selected using a modified Delphi approach. The table of contents from predetermined journals were reviewed and independently evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by paired authors. Pharmacotherapy-related publications deemed to be GRADE 1A and 1B were reviewed by the collective group for inclusion in the review. This article synthesizes and evaluates findings from 7 randomized controlled trials, 10 guidelines, clinical policies, position statements, or consensus recommendations, and 11 meta-analyses, providing critical insight into their potential clinical impact. Covered topics include guideline or policy updates on advanced cardiac life support, rapid sequence intubation, tranexamic acid in trauma, acute coronary syndromes, and hypertension. Randomized controlled trials covering sedative use in rapid sequence intubation, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, sodium bicarbonate for severe acidemia and acute kidney injury in the critically ill, and thrombolytic therapy beyond traditional time windows for ischemic stroke are also reviewed. Additional topics include nebulized and low-dose ketamine for analgesia, erector spinae plane block for renal colic, two-bag versus three-bag acetylcysteine regimens for acetaminophen overdose, QT prolongation in antipsychotic overdose, and naltrexone for opioid dependence.

articles.title: Beyond the destination: Transfer time and pediatric specialization in severe traumatic brain injury.
Multicompartmental hemorrhage: A high-risk pattern associated with increased risk for progression in TBI patients.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) often requires repeat head computed tomography (CT) imaging to monitor for bleed progression. While prior literature has explored patient-level factors, data on the impact of ICH morphologies (subdural [SDH], epidural [EDH], intraparenchymal [IPH], intraventricular [IVH], and multicompartment hemorrhage [MCH]) on radiographic ICH progression remains unclear. We hypothesized that MCH and IVH would have an increased associated risk of progression.

**METHODS**: This retrospective (2021-2023) single-center cohort included adults (≥18 y) with TBI-related ICH who underwent initial and repeat head CT. Patients were stratified into radiographic progression versus no-progression cohorts, with progression defined as new or enlarging hemorrhage on attending radiologist interpretation of follow-up head CT. The primary outcome was the rate of radiographic progression for each ICH type. MCH was defined as the presence of two or more ICH types. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between each ICH type and radiographic progression, adjusting for age, mechanism of injury, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival, trauma-bay intubation, and preinjury antithrombotic exposure.

**RESULTS**: Of the 817 patients with ICH on initial head CT and documented repeat CT, 401 (49.1%) had radiographic progression. Patients with progression were younger (58 vs. 62 y, p=0.027), more frequently male (71.3% vs. 63.7%, p=0.020), and had similar antithrombotic exposure (15.2% vs. 14.2%, p=0.678). Craniotomy/craniectomy was more frequent among those with progression (21.2% vs. 8.2%, p<0.001). On multivariable analysis, MCH demonstrated the strongest associated risk for progression (odds ratio [OR] 5.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.36-9.33, p<0.001), whereas IPH (OR 2.02, CI: 0.86-4.75, p=0.108), SDH, EDH, and IVH were not independently associated with radiographic ICH progression.

**CONCLUSIONS**: MCH was independently associated with radiographic ICH progression. This higher-risk hemorrhage pattern may warrant closer neurological monitoring.

**LEVEL OF EVIDENCE**: Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

articles.title: A clinically relevant porcine model of flail chest: Development and multimodal validation.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Flail chest has high mortality, but large-animal models with thoracic anatomy comparable to humans are lacking. The objective of this study was to develop a clinically relevant porcine flail chest model that preserves pleural, pulmonary, and neurovascular integrity, and to validate it using multimodal assessment including computed tomography (CT) imaging and physiologic parameters.

**METHODS**: Twelve male Landrace pigs were randomly assigned to a flail chest (FC) group and a multiple single rib fracture (MRF) group (n=6 per group). Under general anesthesia, controlled osteotomies were performed on the fifth to eighth ribs. The intercostal neurovascular bundle was protected, and the parietal pleura was bluntly separated before each osteotomy to preserve pleural integrity. In the FC group, each rib was transected at two sites to create a four-rib flail segment; in the MRF group, a single transection was made per rib. Paradoxical chest wall motion was visually confirmed in the FC group before layered closure. Invasive arterial pressure, heart rate, pulse oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and end‑tidal carbon dioxide tension (ETCO₂) were monitored throughout. Chest CT was performed on Day 7.

**RESULTS**: All surgeries were successful, with no mortality. Paradoxical chest wall motion was confirmed in all FC animals after emergence. The SpO₂/FiO₂ ratio declined postoperatively in both groups, with a significantly greater decrease in the FC group than in the MRF group (221.0±1.4 vs. 260.2±1.9, P<0.001). Heart rate and mean arterial pressure increased in both groups and were significantly higher in the FC group (P<0.001). CT confirmed the intended fracture patterns and flail-segment displacement, with no evidence of pleural breach, pulmonary injury, pneumothorax, or hemothorax.

**CONCLUSIONS**: A standardized porcine flail chest model was established that preserves pleural, pulmonary, and neurovascular integrity, allowing the isolated study of rib fracture pathophysiology. This model will facilitate future research on fixation materials and surgical techniques.

**STUDY TYPE**: Basic Science/ Animal Study.

articles.title: Contemporary management of traumatic abdominal wall hernias: What you need to know.
articles.abstract: Traumatic abdominal wall hernia (TAWH) is an uncommon but clinically important consequence of both blunt and penetrating abdominal trauma. It is defined by disruption of the abdominal wall musculature and fascia with herniation of intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal contents through the defect. Although penetrating abdominal wall defects are usually apparent and can often be primarily closed during operative exploration, blunt TAWH is significantly more heterogeneous and challenging. The skin may remain intact while the muscle, fascia, neurovascular supply, and bony attachments are disrupted. The reported incidence of TAWH varies according to imaging strategy and trauma population, but frank herniation remains rare, occurring in <1% of blunt trauma patients in most contemporary series. The major management challenge is deciding whether the patient requires immediate trauma laparotomy or laparoscopy, acute abdominal wall repair, staged management with same-admission repair, or delayed hernia repair/abdominal wall reconstruction. Evidence remains primarily dominated by retrospective single-center series, multicenter registry studies, and systematic reviews with heterogeneous definitions and follow-up. Although traditional dogma had taught that these repairs should always be performed in a delayed fashion, recent multicenter data, systematic reviews, and surgeon experience suggest that timing of repair, type of repair, and mesh use must be individualized; bowel injury, contamination, defect location, and patient physiology are more important than a universal early-versus-delayed algorithm. This article summarizes the practical issues the trauma and acute care surgeon needs to know: diagnosis, classification, associated injuries, indications for exploration, repair timing, operative strategy, management of lateral and posterior defects, mesh use in contaminated fields, and associated outcomes.

articles.title: Pelvic hemorrhage in the context of demographic change: frequency and CT-based characterization of pelvic bleeding.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Traumatic pelvic hemorrhage is a major driver of morbidity and mortality in pelvic fractures. Classic literature described pelvic hemorrhage as predominantly venous, whereas arterial injury is considered less common. We evaluated the frequency, anatomical distribution, and presumed sources of pelvic hemorrhage in a contemporary trauma cohort using contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).

**METHODS**: We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with pelvic fractures treated at a level-I trauma center between 2020 and 2022. All patients underwent CECT at initial presentation. Two experienced pelvic trauma surgeons independently reviewed all scans. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage was defined by contrast extravasation, soft-tissue asymmetry/displacement, or a contained intrapelvic hematoma. Patients with and without hemorrhage were compared regarding age, sex, trauma mechanism, anticoagulation, and fracture type. The presumed bleeding sources were categorized as arterial, venous, cancellous, or mixed.

**RESULTS**: Radiologically relevant hemorrhage occurred in 95/512 (18.6%) patients and was more frequent after high-energy trauma and in men. Iliac sites predominated, whereas presacral bleeding was uncommon. The presumed bleeding source was cancellous in 44.2%, mixed in 29.5%, arterial in 18.9%, and isolated venous in 7.4%. Overall mortality was 7.0% and was significantly higher in patients with hemorrhage (14.7% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001).

**CONCLUSION**: In this contemporary CECT-based cohort, pelvic hemorrhage was less frequent than historically reported, with CT findings most commonly suggesting cancellous or mixed bleeding sources. These findings suggest that the traditional concept of predominantly venous pelvic hemorrhage may not fully reflect current CT-based observations.

articles.title: The new trochanteric nail TFN-A has a higher complication rate in the treatment of proximal femoral fractures than the predecessor model PFN-A.
articles.abstract:
**AIMS**: Trochanteric fractures (TF) are among the most frequent fractures and have major impact on the affected patients and the healthcare system. Cephalomedullary nails (CMN) are widely used for these fractures. Complications remain frequent, either due to comorbidities or concerning the implant. The goal of this retrospective, single-centre study was to compare the complication rates of two CMN from one manufacturer.

**MATERIALS AND METHODS**: All internal fixations TF performed between 01/2017 and 07/2021 in our institution were analysed retrospectively. Follow-up was at least two years. The CMN were the PFN-A or the TFN-A. Demographic data, all reoperations and revisions were recorded. Reoperations and revisions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with subgrouping as minor reoperation, minor revision or major revision, including conversion to total hip arthroplasty.

**RESULTS**: A total of 492 CMN, used in 475 patients, could be included. Among these, 248 were PFN-A and 244 were TFN-A. The overall reoperation rate was 15%, 12.9% for the PFN-A and 17.2% for the TFN-A, respectively. The TFN-A group had significantly more major revisions (hazard ratio 3.57 (95% confidence interval 1.42-9.94; p = 0.004). No relevant differences were found regarding demographic data or the quality of reduction and internal fixation.

**DISCUSSION**: The TFN-A had a significantly higher rate of complications leading to major revision than the former PFN-A. This may have been missed when considering only the reoperation rate for all causes due to a camouflage effect by minor complications.

articles.title: Beyond Survival: Recovery After Traumatic Injury, Does Time Do the Trick?
Acute hemorrhagic shock from vaginal laceration during intercourse requiring operative management.
articles.abstract: Vaginal laceration during consensual intercourse is a rare cause of acute vaginal bleeding. Most coital injuries are minor, although may result in acute hemorrhage and hemodynamic instability. A 30-year-old G3P2012 otherwise healthy woman presented to the emergency department (ED) with acute vaginal bleeding immediately during consensual intercourse. She was initially well-appearing then developed hemorrhagic shock in the ED from ongoing vaginal exsanguination. The bleeding source could not be visualized on speculum examination. She was resuscitated with tranexamic acid, crystalloid, and two units of unmatched whole blood and taken emergently to the operating room. Examination under anesthesia after evacuation identified a horizontal posterior vaginal wall laceration. The laceration was repaired transvaginally with hemostasis, and the patient recovered uneventfully. A vaginal laceration during intercourse may cause acute life-threatening hemorrhage. Bleeding is often occult on speculum examinations although may progress rapidly to shock. Emergency clinicians should exclude pregnancy, initiate early resuscitation, and urgently consult gynecology for examination under anesthesia and repair when indicated.

articles.title: Association of neighborhood social vulnerability with reoperation after operative treatment of proximal humerus fractures.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Neighborhood-level indices may capture different dimensions of social risk. We evaluated whether the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) was associated with reoperation after operative treatment of acute proximal humerus fractures (PHFs), using the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) as a secondary comparator.

**METHODS**: This retrospective cohort included 438 distinct fracture episodes treated within a single United States practice group from January 2021 through December 2024. The outcome was ipsilateral shoulder reoperation for a postoperative complication. Primary logistic regression models adjusted for age, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, and diabetes mellitus; ADI analyses included 414 fractures.

**RESULTS**: Fifty-one fractures (11.6%) underwent reoperation. Reoperation increased from 6.4% to 16.1% across SVI quartiles (ordered trend P = 0.028; omnibus P = 0.163). Each 0.10 increase in SVI was associated with reoperation in the primary model (odds ratio [OR], 1.13; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.26; P = 0.033) and after adjustment for procedure category (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.01-1.26; P = 0.027). ADI national and state ranks were not associated with reoperation.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Higher SVI was associated with reoperation, whereas ADI national and state ranks were not. These index-specific, hypothesis-generating findings require external validation.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
articles.abstract:
**IMPORTANCE**: Female patients undergoing cardiac surgery have a higher transfusion burden, yet they remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. Although the ANH trial showed no significant reduction in the proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusions with acute normovolemic hemodilution, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety specifically in female patients remains limited.

**OBJECTIVE**: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) compared with usual care in female patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

**DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS**: This was a post hoc secondary analysis of the multicenter, randomized ANH trial, which was conducted at 32 centers in 11 countries from April 2019 to December 2024. Of 2010 patients in the original ANH trial, 405 were women and were included in this analysis; 219 had been randomized to receive ANH and 186 to usual care. This secondary analysis was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026.

**INTERVENTION**: Withdrawal of at least 650 mL whole blood with crystalloids replacement and reinfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass.

**MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES**: The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least 1 allogeneic packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion during the index hospitalization. Safety outcomes included intraoperative hypotension, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, and other perioperative complications.

**RESULTS**: The median (IQR) age of the participants was 62 (54-69) years. The occurrence of allogeneic pRBC transfusion was similar in the ANH and usual care groups (38.8% vs 44.6%, respectively; relative risk [RR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.69-1.10; P = .24). Intraoperative hypotension occurred more frequently with ANH (16.0% vs 4.8% in usual care; RR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74; P = .02). Patients receiving ANH also had longer ICU stays (mean difference, 21.13 hours; 95% CI, 1.89-40.38; P = .03) and hospital stays (mean difference, 1.92 days; 95% CI, 0.14-3.70; P = .04). No significant differences were observed in mortality or other postoperative complications.

**CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE**: In this post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, ANH was not associated with a reduction in allogeneic pRBC transfusion among women undergoing cardiac surgery and was associated with more frequent intraoperative hypotension and longer ICU and hospital stay. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies specifically designed to evaluate female patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

**TRIAL REGISTRATION**: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03913481.

Comparison of two immobilization techniques for radiological outcomes in fifth metacarpal neck fractures: a prospective controlled study.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Although fifth metacarpal neck fractures are commonly managed conservatively, there is no consensus regarding the optimal immobilization strategy. The aim of this study was to compare the radiographic outcomes of the Jahss Position Splint (JPS) and the conventional Ulnar Gutter Splint (UGS) in the treatment of fifth metacarpal neck fractures.

**METHODS**: A total of 78 adult male patients treated for isolated closed fifth metacarpal neck fractures between January 2023 and June 2024 were prospectively evaluated. Patients were allocated to either the JPS group (n = 42) or the UGS group (n = 36). Patients were assigned to JPS or UGS according to the predefined odd/even-calendar-day duty schedule of two surgeons, each of whom routinely applied one of the techniques. All patients underwent closed reduction using the Jahss maneuver followed by three weeks of immobilization. Radiographic outcomes included initial fracture angulation (IFA), post-reduction angulation (PRA), final follow-up angulation at 12 weeks (FFA), metacarpal shortening, and malunion rates.

**RESULTS**: No significant differences were observed between the groups regarding age or IFA (p > 0.05). Correction during reduction and splint application was greater with JPS than with UGS (15.2 ± 9.6° vs. 8.9 ± 11.0°; p = 0.009), whereas subsequent loss of reduction during immobilisation did not differ significantly between the groups (2.8 ± 8.4° vs. 1.0 ± 9.8°; p = 0.388).The JPS group demonstrated significantly lower PRA (p < 0.001) and FFA (p = 0.003) compared with the UGS group. Metacarpal shortening was significantly less in the JPS group (p = 0.036). The malunion rate was 5% in the JPS group and 28% in the UGS group (p = 0.009).

**CONCLUSION**: JPS was associated with greater immediate angular correction and more favourable final radiographic outcomes than UGS but did not reduce subsequent loss of reduction during immobilisation. Because functional and patient-reported outcomes were not assessed, the clinical relevance of these radiographic differences remains uncertain.

articles.title: Surgical management of orbital wall fractures in juveniles: a European multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
**INTRODUCTION**: Isolated orbital floor fractures in juveniles are a challenge, as children and adolescents may experience diplopia and limited ocular motility, even with little to no periorbital edema or visible signs of injury to the eye. The aim of the present study is to assess the demographic and clinical variables, and the outcomes of pediatric patients affected by isolated orbital wall fractures at several European oral and maxillofacial surgery centers.

**METHODS**: Pediatric patients (less than 18 years) with hospitalized and surgically treated for unilateral isolated orbital blow out fractures of the orbital floor and/or the medial wall were included. The following data were recorded for each patient: gender, age, etiology of trauma, site of orbital wall fracture(s), timing of intervention, surgical approach, orbital reconstruction material/implant, post-operative complications RESULTS: A total of 51 pediatric patients (45 boys, 6 girls) with a mean age of 12.1 years were included. Most patients (43 children, 84.3%) presented with an isolated orbital floor fracture. Clinically, the most frequently observed sign was diplopia / double vision (43 patients, 84.3%). More than two thirds (68.6%) of cases were surgically treated within the first two days from injury. In 6 patients (11.8%) one or more persistent postoperative disturbances were found six months postoperatively, including diplopia in 3 subjects (5.9%), infraorbital nerve paresthesia in 2 patients (3.9%), and enophthalmos in 2 patients (3.9%).

**CONCLUSIONS**: The rarity of pure orbital wall fractures in pediatric patients makes it difficult to establish uniform evidence-based guidelines for their management. These injuries must also be recognized promptly, as surgical intervention may be required at a very early stage. A reasoned and individualized choice of the optimal surgical approach appears to be the most appropriate strategy for this specific type of facial fracture in the pediatric population.

**CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER**: Not applicable.

articles.title: Management and outcomes of moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures: a 10-year experience from an Australian Level 1 Trauma Centre.
articles.abstract:
**PURPOSE**: Moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures are associated with high morbidity and mortality despite advances in resuscitation, development in trauma systems and multispecialty haemorrhage control. This study aimed to describe the management strategies and clinical outcomes of moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures over a 10-year period at an Australian Level I Trauma Centre.

**METHODS**: A retrospective observational cohort study was performed of patients aged ≥ 16 years with moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures (Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) ≥ 3) treated between January 2015 and December 2024. Data were obtained from the institutional prospectively collected trauma registry.

**RESULTS**: A total of 313 patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 47.0 years and 69.3% were male. Motor vehicle (35.1%) and motorcycle collisions (24.9%) accounted for 60.1% of injuries. Median ISS was 26 (IQR 19-34), with 70.6% sustaining pelvic AIS 4-5 injuries. 20.1% of patients underwent at least one haemorrhage-control intervention, including angioembolisation (14.4%), preperitoneal pelvic packing (5.8%) and external fixation (5.8%). Angioembolisation utilisation increased from 6.7% in 2015 to 40.0% in 2024. In-hospital mortality was 7.7%, with traumatic brain injury accounting for 62.5% of deaths and haemorrhagic shock for only one death.

**CONCLUSION**: Moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures remained characterised by high-energy mechanisms and severe multisystem injury over the study period, while management evolved with increasing utilisation of angioembolisation. In-hospital mortality was numerically lower compared with historical cohorts, with most deaths attributable to associated traumatic brain injury rather than pelvic haemorrhage.

articles.title: Early cystography after traumatic bladder repair: Diagnostic intervention or marker of an accelerated catheter removal pathway?
Prehospital Care of Older Adults Following Perceived Low-Acuity Falls and Related "Lift Assist" Encounters: An NAEMSP Position Statement and Resource Document.
articles.abstract: Older adults who present as low-acuity falls requiring mobilization assistance, commonly referred to as a "lift assist", represent a common reason for EMS activation. These encounters often involve underlying medical conditions or injuries that are not immediately apparent, and missed or delayed diagnosis is associated with adverse outcomes. At the same time, some patients are transported to the emergency department when it is not necessary, exposing them to potential harms and contributing to increased healthcare utilization. These encounters are therefore complex clinical presentations and represent important opportunities for thorough assessment and higher-order clinical decision making, supported by systems that enable appropriate disposition and follow-up. However, there is a system-level bias, beginning in initial education and reinforced through dispatch, policy, and protocol, that frames these encounters as uniformly low-acuity, non-medical, minor traumas leading to underassessment and limiting clinical decision-making. Therefore, NAEMSP recommends:EMS systems should recognize calls for falls or "lift assists" as patient encounters that warrant an assessment, including evaluation for underlying medical causes, traumatic injuries, and safety, and frame these encounters as opportunities for higher-order clinical decision-making within the broader context of geriatric syndromes rather than isolated low-acuity events.EMS systems should support transport decisions based on a thorough assessment and patient-centered discussion, recognizing that not all patients require ED transport and that safe alternatives may include non-transport or referral to appropriate follow-up pathways.EMS systems should track the assessment of patients encountered during "lift assist" responses and older adults following perceived low acuity falls as a system-level quality measure to monitor performance and drive improvement.Policymakers and payers should implement sustainable reimbursement structures that support EMS assessment and care even when transport does not occur.

articles.title: Moving diagnostics upstream: prehospital blood gas analysis is associated with safe community care and improved patient selection for hospital admission.
Rhabdo-RRT score: development and external validation of an emergency department tool for predicting renal replacement therapy in rhabdomyolysis.
Shoulder anterior capsular (SHAC) block for analgesia in anterior shoulder dislocation: An emergency department case series.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Anterior shoulder dislocation is among the most common major joint dislocations presenting to the emergency department (ED) and is frequently managed with procedural sedation. Several analgesic and regional anesthesia strategies are available for shoulder reduction, each with distinct advantages and limitations. The Shoulder Anterior Capsular (SHAC) block is a superficial, ultrasound-guided interfascial plane technique that targets pericapsular nerve contributions to the glenohumeral joint via an anterior approach, offering a potentially motor-sparing and sedation-sparing alternative.

**CASE PRESENTATION**: We present two cases of ED anterior shoulder dislocation managed with the SHAC block at a high-volume Level 1 trauma center. In the first case, a 60-year-old male with recurrent dislocation underwent successful reduction without procedural sedation, reporting it as his least painful reduction among multiple prior experiences. In the second case, a 94-year-old female with a complex fracture-dislocation in cervical spine precautions received the SHAC block as an analgesic adjunct; although procedural sedation was ultimately required, the patient required no intravenous analgesia during a subsequent 36-h observation period. In both cases, the block was performed by an emergency medicine intern under supervision by a Pain Medicine fellowship-trained attending physician, preserving the ability to conduct post-reduction axillary nerve assessment.

**CONCLUSION**: The SHAC block was technically feasible in two selected patients with anterior shoulder dislocation and provided variable analgesia. Further study is needed to evaluate its efficacy, safety, positioning requirements, reproducibility, and appropriate patient selection.

articles.title: Does Time Truly Heal All? A Prospective Cohort Study of 6- To 12-Month Recovery Transitions After Traumatic Injury.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Recovery after traumatic injury may extend beyond conventional follow-up, but longer-term changes in function, quality of life (QoL), and return to work (RTW) remain incompletely characterized.

**STUDY DESIGN**: English- or Spanish-speaking patients with Injury Severity Score ≥9 from three US Level I trauma centers completed telephone surveys 6 and 12 months after injury. Recovery was characterized as improved, stable, or declined between timepoints. Function was assessed across six Trauma Quality of Life domains; QoL and RTW by self-report; and mental health using GAD-7, PHQ-8, and Breslau PTSD scales. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated predictors of QoL decline. Sensitivity analyses examined traumatic brain injury (TBI), isolated long bone fracture, and general trauma.

**RESULTS**: Among 1,894 patients, 49% of those impaired at 6 months improved, 41% were unchanged, and 11% worsened by 12 months. Patients ≥65 more often improved (20% vs. 16%) and declined (16% vs. 9%) than those <65; surgical patients more often improved (20% vs. 16%). QoL improved in 22%, remained stable in 56%, and declined in 22%. TBI patients had the greatest functional improvement (55%), whereas long bone fracture patients had the greatest QoL improvement (26%). Weak social support (aOR 3.68) and mental health symptoms were associated with QoL decline. RTW reached 61% by 6 months; 74% of non-returners remained so at 12 months.

**CONCLUSIONS**: Recovery remains dynamic beyond 6 months after trauma, supporting extended follow-up and individualized rehabilitation. Associations of mental health symptoms and weak social support with QoL decline support incorporating their assessment into post-injury care.

articles.title: Creation of a formal chest wall injury program improves compliance with rib fixation indications.
articles.abstract:
**BACKGROUND**: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) improves outcomes but remains underutilized. This study evaluated the impact of the creation of a dedicated, institutional chest wall injury program on SSRF utilization, hypothesizing such a program would increase utilization of SSRF for those patients meeting criteria.

**METHODS**: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study of adults with radiographically confirmed rib fractures presenting to a Level I trauma center between January 2016 and April 2023.
